title: Nine dead in mass shooting in Thailand. Here's how it unfolded.

Topic:Shootings

A student reacts after evacuating from Debsirin Nonthaburi School, following the shooting. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

The Thai Prime Minister has vowed to introduce a new firearms control law after a teenager killed nine people at a high school and a home outside Bangkok.

Police say the 14-year-old shooter then turned the gun on himself.

More details have emerged about how the tragedy unfolded. Here's what we know.

Readers are advised this article contains details that may be distressing.

A Thai police official said the shooting started at around 5am local time when the boy killed his grandparents in their two-storey house on the outskirts of Bangkok.

Forensic police experts work at the site of a residence, where a Thai teenager fatally shot his grandparents. (Reuters: Tananchai Keawsowattana)

Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong, superintendent of Bang Bua Thong Police Station, told Reuters: "The firearm and the bullets belonged to the grandfather.

"An initial inspection found signs that the firearm had been searched for inside the grandfather's bedroom."

The three of them lived together in the house in Bang Bua Thong, in a quiet neighbourhood, a 90-minute drive from central Bangkok.

Police say the teenager then took school transport as normal, and headed to Debsirin Nonthaburi School.

His first class began at 8:30am, followed by another at 9:20am.

About half an hour into the boy's second class of the day he drew out the gun and began shooting again.

The teenager is believed to have first shot teachers on the sixth floor of the building where he studied, killing three of them, police said.

The gunman then appears to have continued down a corridor, shooting at students.

Police say in all, the boy used at least 26 bullets. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

Two other staff members were attacked and killed on a staircase.

Police got a call about a shooting at 9:57am.

Students have described how they ran out of the school in their socks or bare feet, leaving their shoes behind.

Police cleared the building floor-by-floor and found the teenager on the fourth floor, where he had already shot himself.

Belongings left behind by evacuated students lie next to a pillar with a bullet marking in the building where the shooting incident began. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

The time was around 10:40am.

Police say he was still alive, so they performed CPR and rushed him to the hospital.

The 14-year-old died soon after.

When he arrived at the school, emergency worker Kiatikhun Verapongpradith said the scene was chaotic as his team began treating students with wounds to the back, chest and arms.

A relative of a victim reacts outside Debsirin Nonthaburi School. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

"We were evaluating the sort of weapons he had," he said, referring to the gunman.

"Therefore, we could not rush inside. The police then took a team with shields up there."

At least 23 people were wounded in the shooting. (Reuters: Athit Perawongmetha)

The boy's motives remain unclear.

"He was stressed from his studies," Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters after he visited the school.

"This is terrible for something like this to happen," he said.

"I'm sad for those who died and sad for something like this to happen in our country."

A forensic marking of the impact from a bullet on the bottom of a pillar. (Reuters: Chalinee Thirasupa)

The student was also described by police as "quiet, not very sociable, and fairly good academically".

Friday's rampage was Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022.

What happened has renewed scrutiny of gun regulations in Thailand, Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation with roughly 15 firearms per 100 residents.

This compares with less than one per 100 in neighbouring Malaysia

Mr Anutin, who tightened gun laws when he was interior minister following a previous mass shooting, said he will propose a new law to restrict the carrying of firearms by the public.

"As much as possible, we have to create an atmosphere of safety," he said.
